source_checks.claim: PI05 recipe uses fixed-graph DDP settings: find_unused_parameters=False, static_graph=True, gradient_as_bucket_view=True. It recommends disabling the outer suffix checkpoint; internal checkpointing remains.; The documented stable interval is about 5.75–5.85 s/it for the supplied recipe; this is a source claim rather than this target measurement.
source_checks.comparison: DDP bucketing and fixed graph are design references. The recipe is not a replacement for independent, leased fragment tasks. Conditions: LeRobot/Accelerate PI05 recipe, example nproc=2, internal gradient checkpointing enabled.; Grouped MLP benefits explicitly include backward recomputation. Contrary evidence: Disabling only the outer checkpoint does not satisfy the user requirement that all activation recomputation be disabled.; Published timings and grouped-MLP gains cannot be transferred to this OpenPI execution path or 32 preemptible NPUs. Remaining gaps: Recipe does not cover independent worker loss/replacement or full shared-filesystem gradient exchange.

source_checks.claim: The three settings are passed into DistributedDataParallelKwargs on an Accelerator.; Accelerator backward synchronizes the gradients; each rank owns an optimizer and steps it locally.; The explicit pin_memory condition is device.type == cuda, so this source does not itself prove a working NPU pinned-host transfer implementation.
source_checks.comparison: Provides actual call-site evidence for the recipe DDP claims, not a direct transport replacement. Conditions: Fixed Accelerator process group and identical local optimizer evolution are assumed.; The file locally redefines _resolve_ddp_settings and calls _env_flag without defining/importing that helper in this file; static reading alone does not establish standalone execution. Contrary evidence: It has no CPU authority that publishes a new full model version per update.; Its source pin_memory setting is insufficient evidence for Ascend pinned staging. Remaining gaps: This source was not executed; exact environment integration and helper availability were not evaluated.

source_checks.claim: Both all_gather_into_tensor calls have async_op=True; local attention runs before both handles are waited; gathered K/V are consumed only afterward.; Other communication paths explicitly synchronize and use blocking all_to_all_single; the file does not make all communication asynchronous.
source_checks.comparison: Actual Ascend overlap example. Its buffer and work-handle lifetime ordering is relevant to a new bounded transport pipeline. Conditions: Each process has valid fixed Ulysses/Ring groups; number of heads divisible by Ulysses group size; compatible tensor shapes/dtypes; inference FIA/LSE support. Contrary evidence: Group membership remains fixed. It is not a failure-tolerant fragment protocol. Remaining gaps: No execution here; no guarantee of overlap or gains on target device/version.

source_checks.claim: Ring strategy submits asynchronous K/V all-gathers, performs independent local attention, waits, then consumes remote tensors.; Reported parallel speedups belong to eight-card Atlas 800I A2 VGGT inference on 25 kitchen images.
source_checks.comparison: Supports the submit-independent-work-wait ordering pattern, not PI05 backward correctness. Conditions: Inference, sequence parallelism, fixed ring process group, NPU fused inference attention with LSE. Contrary evidence: Fused infer attention path is not evidence of a trainable/autograd implementation.; The BF16 text says 0.919 to 0.911 and also claims less than 0.5% loss; the stated numbers do not support that percentage. No precision inference is adopted from it. Remaining gaps: No elastic gradient buckets, CPU reducers, or arbitrary rank dropout validation.

source_checks.claim: hash.update represents hashing the concatenation of provided buffers; GIL is released when more than 2047 bytes are supplied at once.
source_checks.comparison: Independent large chunk hashes can use Python threads; combining chunk digests is a distinct protocol rather than plain whole-payload SHA256. Conditions: CPython 3.11.10 source documentation; actual target interpreter/hash backend must be checked. Contrary evidence: This does not make a single ordered SHA256 stream parallel by updating one shared object from unordered tasks. Remaining gaps: No speed measurement or actual target hashlib backend inspection.

source_checks.claim: For buffers >= HASHLIB_GIL_MINSIZE an object lock is allocated; EVP_hash runs inside Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS while holding that hash object lock.; The implementation includes hashlib.h, which defines the threshold.
source_checks.comparison: Confirms that parallel independent hashes may execute off the GIL. Conditions: OpenSSL-backed CPython implementation, large buffers, independent hash object per independent chunk. Contrary evidence: Sharing one hash object serializes updates with its lock and does not define desired chunk ordering. Remaining gaps: Target Python build/provider and memory-bandwidth saturation not measured.

source_checks.claim: The threshold is exactly 2048 bytes.
source_checks.comparison: Supports selecting chunks well above the GIL-release threshold. Conditions: Same full CPython commit as calling implementation. Contrary evidence:  Remaining gaps:

source_checks.claim: Explicit-offset reads/writes leave the descriptor file offset unchanged; pwrite returns the number of bytes actually written.; Successful same-filesystem rename/replace is atomic; crossing filesystems may fail.
source_checks.comparison: Supports bounded parallel I/O to distinct offsets and publishing completed immutable payloads using atomic replacement. Conditions: Unix/POSIX semantics; handle short reads/writes and complete all chunk tasks before publishing the descriptor. Contrary evidence: Atomic rename is not a payload checksum, a durability guarantee, or proof of shared-filesystem cache coherency/scaling. Remaining gaps: Actual shared-filesystem implementation, caching, durability, and physical throughput not measured.

source_checks.claim: Many numeric NumPy operations release the GIL; easiest safe parallelism uses thread-owned arrays or read-only shared inputs; concurrent mutation/read can cause races or crashes.; dtype=object operations do not release the GIL.
source_checks.comparison: A CPU reducer can parallelize disjoint output ranges while sharing immutable source buffers. Conditions: NumPy 2.1.0; normal numeric dtypes, no Python-object loops; actual installed version not reverified by this investigation. Contrary evidence: Multiple threads must not concurrently write or resize the same output region. Remaining gaps: No benchmark; useful thread count depends on CPU allocation, memory bandwidth, other reducer/I/O threads.

source_checks.claim: The selected strided_loop runs between NPY_BEGIN_THREADS_THRESHOLDED(count) and NPY_END_THREADS when NPY_METH_REQUIRES_PYAPI is absent.
source_checks.comparison: Confirms the implementation mechanism behind potential CPU FP32 multiply/add parallelism. Conditions: Loop has compatible strides and no Python API requirement; numeric array method; large enough loop for threshold. Contrary evidence: Changing source aggregation order or using a reduction tree can change FP32 rounding even if threading is race-free. This numeric-order statement is an algorithmic inference, not a NumPy speed claim. Remaining gaps: This investigation did not run or benchmark the installed NumPy loop.

source_checks.claim: Autograd readiness triggers asynchronous bucket allreduce; all ranks invoke collectives in the same bucket index order; optimizer runs after reduction completion.
source_checks.comparison: Conceptual motivation for ready-bucket overlap; implementation-critical details were cross-checked against v2.8.0 C++ sources. Conditions: Document explicitly warns that its design note is based on v1.4, despite being retrieved at v2.8.0 commit. Contrary evidence: Historical implementation links in the document point to v1.7.0; these were not treated as the v2.8.0 implementation. Remaining gaps: No actual HCCL backend or elastic group behavior established by this note.

source_checks.claim: Initialization synchronizes parameter state; normal training relies on every rank applying the same averaged gradient with the same optimizer, rather than rebroadcasting all parameters each update.; Bucketing can overlap reduction with backward; gradient_as_bucket_view removes gradient/bucket copies after first iteration; static_graph requires stable used/unused parameter sets and training flow.; Join mode selects an authoritative rank and synchronizes the final model.
source_checks.comparison: Explains why a fast fixed-group backend can avoid repeated full-model parameter exchange, but current single CPU Adam authority cannot skip publication under that assumption. Conditions: Identical local optimizer evolution, process group collective participation and ordering; static graph assumptions must hold. Contrary evidence: Join-mode authoritative final-model selection is not crash recovery for arbitrary killed workers.; Same-device gradient bucket views do not prove CPU-to-NPU pinned staging. Remaining gaps: Actual torch_npu/HCCL backend needs separate device/version checks and restart design.

source_checks.claim: A worker failure stops/restarts all workers; node arrival/departure forms a new worker group after stopping existing workers.; Ranks/world size may change and ranks must not be treated as stable identities.
source_checks.comparison: Counterevidence to treating ordinary elastic DDP as independent fragment-worker replacement. Conditions: torchrun elastic worker-group semantics; homogeneous local worker count. Contrary evidence: The group-restart model can discard work of surviving workers; target fragment protocol currently preserves admitted atomic work via leases/fences. Remaining gaps: No QZ preemption integration or target correctness/performance validated.

source_checks.claim: All participating ranks must provide tensors with the same element count; async_op returns the group work handle, otherwise it waits.
source_checks.comparison: Can carry a versioned flat parameter bucket inside a deliberately managed group. Conditions: A valid process group/backend, matching collective source/shape/order, safe tensor lifetime until completion. Contrary evidence: The generic API provides no generation/attempt fencing and no dynamic replacement guarantee. Remaining gaps: HCCL CPU/device constraints and target parameter-service membership remain outside this source.

source_checks.claim: Ready buckets are launched in bucket index order; it stops at the first not-ready bucket.; Each bucket stores future_work; finalization waits before unpacking the completed result.
source_checks.comparison: Actual current code supports submit-ready-bucket and defer final wait, while preserving order and consumption boundaries. Conditions: Fixed matching process group; safe stream ordering and completed gradients; source itself notes non-default-stream event synchronization concerns. Contrary evidence: No independent sample leasing or immutable source-commit protocol exists in this reducer. Remaining gaps: Need target-specific backward completion hooks and failure recovery; none executed here.

source_checks.claim: Same-device/same-dtype tensors are flattened into a bucket; work is waited before unflattening and copy-back.; The implementation bounds in-flight bucket broadcasts to two to control memory.
source_checks.comparison: Useful reference for dtype-aware flattening, bounded in-flight buffers, explicit wait/lifetime management. Conditions: Matching group participants, same device and dtype within a bucket, owned storage retained through completion. Contrary evidence: Copy-back non_blocking=True is same-device bucket handling, not proof that pageable CPU-to-NPU transfer is asynchronous. Remaining gaps: No direct target speed or HCCL support evidence.
